label: Evidence about the production of a particular epistemic verdict
term: Basis-specific audit of a verdict's production
definition: For a supplied reliability frame an audit assigns each basis its cross-history judgment profile and a report about how that basis produced its verdict in the target class. The interpreted report says a cue determined the output while bypassing the specified comparison. A primitive relation says the subject actually uses a reporting basis for this report and the grounds it supplies are adequate without the operation under investigation. The audited-bypass condition requires acceptance and warrant for the report and an undefeated supporting basis standing in this relation. The policy adds fixed correctness and cross-history variation before it treats the target basis as undercut.
note: Analyst interpretation for #1615. The report is a supplied content. Neither its intended subject matter nor genuinely independent provenance follows from a label or different basis identity. The investigator must identify the operation, history variation, relied-on sources, residual proxy information and admissible case class. No undercut, distribution, reliability or global conclusion is built into report warrant.
